observations.observation: Ein C-12-Atom shows 12 u and approximately 2.0 times 10^-23 g. 1 mol C-12-Atome shows approximately 7.2 times 10^24 u and approximately 12 g. The bottom statement expressly says both units apply to both samples.

12 u is correct for one C-12 atom by definition of u. Approximately 2.0 times 10^-23 g is the appropriate mass scale. For one mol of these atoms, 12 times 6.02214076 times 10^23 gives 7.226568912 times 10^24 u, consistent with the rounded 7.2 times 10^24 u. Approximately 12 g avoids the post-2019 exact-molar-mass shortcut.
The arrow specifies particle number times particle mass. It therefore connects the change in particle number to total mass without defining u or g as exclusive to either level.

The finite pile is explicitly labelled schematisch immediately below the atoms. Each sphere is marked C-12. The label is clearly visible at full size and at both supplied 360/680 pixel previews; the pile is not presented as the literal count of one mol.

All rounded gram/sample values display the approximation sign. The individual-atom gram line has a visible minus sign in the exponent -23. The portion u line has positive exponent 24. Neither sign nor exponent is clipped.

The 360 pixel preview keeps the one-atom and one-mol headings, both rows of units and values, the connecting rule, schematic marker and concluding claim recognisable. The exponent is small but legible; no main information is removed or overlapped.
At 680 pixels the same labels and four mass values are readable with clear exponent/approximation notation. The graphic hierarchy distinguishes particle, portion and multiplication relationship.
